variables.claim_asserts: At a given length, related fishes' body depth and width vary inversely, limiting variation in volume and hence W/L^3.
variables.test_measures: Within-family association of ln(maximum body depth/standard length) and ln(maximum fish width/standard length), plus dispersion of ln(mass/standard length cubed).

modality.note: Same-specimen three-dimensional morphometrics and mass directly supply the transverse dimensions and Thompson's length-weight coefficient.

assumptions.note: Family-centring operationalizes related fishes, and geometric species means compare shape at standardized length; preservation may add noise but does not change the measured variables.

scope.claim_scope: Related fish species differing in body depth and width, including haddock/plaice and shark/skate examples.
scope.test_scope: 5,670 teleost species in 195 families with at least five measured species; sharks and skates are absent.

reasons: Maximum body depth, maximum fish width, standard length, and mass are the variables named by the claim rather than proxies for unrelated morphology.
Family-centred Spearman rho = 0.5274 tests the asserted inverse depth-width variation among related species and finds the opposite sign.
SD of centred ln k is 0.3467, exceeding both depth-ratio SD 0.2165 and width-ratio SD 0.1777, directly testing the claimed conservation of W/L^3.
The named plaice-haddock check also uses the author's quantities, though it is descriptive and the broad verdict appropriately rests on the preregistered teleost analysis.
what_would_change_it: Use matched live or fresh specimens across related species, including elasmobranch examples, and show negative depth-width covariation with ln(mass/length cubed) less variable than both transverse ratios.
